tool.name: pathotypr predict
tool.description: assigns lineages to genomes using a trained model

param.name: input
param.label: Genomes to classify
param.help: A FASTA of sequences with unknown lineage. Headers are reported back unchanged.

param.name: model
param.label: Trained model
param.help: Produced by pathotypr train. A pre-trained model for the M. tuberculosis complex is on Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.19210044.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`pathotypr predict` applies a model built by *pathotypr train* to new sequences. It streams the input in batches, so memory stays flat regardless of how many genomes you give it.
The output has one row per input sequence:
========================= ==================================================== Column Meaning ========================= ==================================================== ``Header`` The FASTA header of the input sequence, unchanged ``Predicted_Lineage`` The class the ensemble voted for ``Confidence`` Fraction of trees that voted for it, 0 to 1 ``Confidence_Margin`` The gap to the runner-up ``Other_Votes`` The remaining classes and their shares ========================= ====================================================
**Reading the confidence**
Confidence is a vote share among the classes the model was trained on, not a probability that the answer is right. A genome from a lineage that was never in the training set will still be assigned to the nearest class it knows, and can do so confidently. The margin is the more useful number of the two: a high confidence with a small margin means two classes were nearly tied.
.. class:: warningmark
A model only knows the labels it was trained on, and those come from the first whitespace-separated token of each header in the training FASTA. If a model was trained on genomes with unedited public-archive headers it will have one class per accession, and its predictions will be meaningless however confident they look.
@ORGANISM_NOTE@
